name: William Davenport

events.title: Children recorded in the Davenport family Bible
events.description: The Bible, presented by Thomas Davenport (1682-1759) to his grandson Thomas on 25 Aug 1759, records that William Davenport of Fordham and his wife Mary (surname not known) had Thomas (1682-1759), William (1683-1735), Francis (1685-1720) and Rachel

bioAdditions: According to the Davenport genealogy, the family Bible gives his children as Thomas (b. 1682, d. 1759), William (b. 1683, d. 1735), Francis (b. 1685, d. 1720) and Rachel, while noting that these four may not be all his children (S1). The Bible was given to a grandson in 1759 and its entries are copies, so it is family evidence, not a contemporary record. The book's chart then names John Davenport and his wife Mary of Long Neck near New Rochelle, said to have come to America in 1670 with four children, as William's parents. The book itself calls that first generation 'a supposition'. Its only document is a deed of 15 Jan 1682/3 in which John Davenport and Mary his wife sold land on Long Neck (NY Hist. Record vol. 45 p.112) (S1). Note that 'came from England in 1670' is told of John and Mary in one place and of William and Mary in another (Bolton).

confidenceRecommendation.justification: The 1718 deed naming Thomas as his son is primary (as cited in the existing bio), and the Bible agrees.

sources.citation: Giles, Thomas Davenport, Pioneer, and His Descendants: family Bible entries; family chart; deed of John Davenport and Mary, 15 Jan 1682/3 (citing NYGBR vol.45 p.112)

openQuestionsNew: John Davenport of Long Neck as his father is called 'a supposition' even by the family genealogy; Westchester deeds or wills of the 1680s-1690s are needed.
researchLogEntry: Round 4: the family Bible (via Giles) gives the children Thomas 1682, William 1683, Francis 1685 and Rachel; the John Davenport of Long Neck parentage is admitted supposition.
